tasks.title: Build a JavaScript Course Status
tasks.description: Create a simple JavaScript program that represents a student's course status using the fundamental JavaScript concepts covered in this module.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that stores a student's name, course name, completed lessons, and total lessons. Calculate the course progress percentage and print a meaningful course status in the console.
objectives: Use JavaScript variables or an object to store related student and course information.
Calculate a percentage using arithmetic operators.
Use JavaScript to produce a meaningful course status.
Display the final result using console.log().
requirements: Store the student's name and course name.
Store completed lessons and total lessons.
Calculate the progress percentage.
Print the student's name, course name, progress percentage, and status.
Use const or let appropriately.
tasks.hint: Use an object to keep the student and course information together. Calculate progress with completedLessons / totalLessons * 100, then use console.log() to display the result.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The student object keeps the related course information together. The progress is calculated using completed lessons divided by total lessons. A conditional expression determines whether the course is completed or still in progress, and console.log() displays the result.

tasks.title: Build a Student Result Calculator
tasks.description: Build a small JavaScript result calculator using variables, primitive values, arithmetic operators, comparisons, logical operators, and explicit type conversion.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that calculates a student's result from three subject marks. The marks are initially provided as strings, so convert them explicitly to numbers. Calculate the total and average, determine whether the student passed all subjects, and print a complete result summary.
objectives: Convert string values into numbers explicitly.
Use arithmetic operators to calculate total and average.
Use comparison and logical operators to determine the result.
Use meaningful variables to represent the student's result.
requirements: Store the student's name.
Store three subject marks as string values.
Convert all marks using Number().
Calculate total marks and average marks.
A subject is passed when its mark is at least 40.
The student passes only when all three subjects are passed.
Print the student name, total, average, and Pass or Fail status.
tasks.hint: Start by converting each mark with Number(). Calculate total and average separately. Check each subject with >= 40 and combine the conditions using &&.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The marks start as strings, so Number() performs explicit type conversion. Arithmetic operators calculate the total and average. Each mark is compared with 40, and the && operator requires all three conditions to be true before the student is considered passed.

tasks.title: Build a Course Enrollment Summary
tasks.description: Build a JavaScript course enrollment summary that combines variables, objects, primitive values, arithmetic, comparisons, logical operators, and explicit type conversion.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that generates a course enrollment summary for a student. The student's age, completed lessons, and total lessons are provided as string values. Convert the numeric values explicitly, validate the data, calculate progress, and print an appropriate enrollment status. If the numeric data is invalid or the total lessons value is zero or negative, print 'Invalid course data' instead.
objectives: Combine the fundamental JavaScript concepts covered in this module.
Use an object to organize student and course information.
Perform explicit type conversion before calculations.
Validate numeric data using comparisons and logical operators.
Calculate course progress and generate a meaningful status.
requirements: Create an object containing student name, age, course name, completed lessons, and total lessons.
Store age, completed lessons, and total lessons as string values initially.
Convert those values explicitly using Number().
Reject the data when any converted numeric value is NaN.
Reject the data when total lessons is zero or negative.
Reject the data when completed lessons is negative or greater than total lessons.
For valid data, calculate the progress percentage.
Print the student name, course name, age, progress, and enrollment status.
tasks.hint: Convert the string values before validation. Number.isNaN() can help detect invalid numeric conversion. Use && and || to combine validation conditions. Only calculate progress after the data passes validation.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The enrollment object stores all related information. Numeric values are explicitly converted with Number(). The validation combines Number.isNaN(), comparison operators, and logical operators to reject invalid data before any percentage calculation occurs. Once valid, progress is calculated and a status is selected according to the progress value.

tasks.title: Build a Student Performance and Role Checker
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript program that evaluates a student's performance and identifies the user's role using conditional logic and a switch statement.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program for a learning platform. Store a student's score and role. First, use if, else if and else to print whether the student has Excellent, Pass or Practice status based on the score. Then use a switch statement to print a message for the role: admin, student or guest.
requirements: Store a numeric student score in a JavaScript variable.
Use if, else if and else to determine the performance status.
Use a switch statement to handle admin, student and guest roles.
Print both the performance status and role message using console.log().
Handle a role that is not recognized with a default case.
objectives: Apply conditional logic to make decisions.
Use switch statements for multiple known cases.
Produce meaningful console output from JavaScript conditions.
tasks.hint: Start with a score variable and check the highest condition first. For the role, use switch(role) with separate cases for admin, student and guest, and include a default case.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The score is evaluated with if, else if and else so only the matching performance level is selected. The role is then handled with switch, where each known role has its own case and break. The default case handles any role that is not recognized.

tasks.title: Build a Course Progress Report
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript course progress report using loops and reusable functions with parameters and return values.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program for a student course containing several lessons. Store the lesson names in an array and the number of completed lessons separately. Use a loop to print every lesson name. Then create a reusable function that accepts completed lessons and total lessons and returns the completion percentage. Finally, print a meaningful course progress report.
requirements: Store multiple lesson names in an array.
Use a loop to print every lesson name.
Create a reusable function with parameters.
Return the calculated completion percentage from the function.
Handle the case where the total number of lessons is zero.
Print the final progress percentage.
objectives: Use loops to repeat an operation over course lessons.
Create reusable functions with parameters.
Use return values to produce calculated results.
Combine loops and functions in a practical JavaScript program.
tasks.hint: Use for...of to iterate through the lesson array. Create a function such as calculateProgress(completed, total) and return 0 when total is zero to avoid an invalid calculation.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The lessons array stores the course lessons and for...of visits each lesson one by one. calculateProgress() receives completed and total as parameters and returns the percentage. The zero-total check prevents division by zero. The returned value is then printed as the course progress.

tasks.title: Build a Course Progress Tracker
tasks.description: Create a reusable course progress tracker using arrow functions, callbacks and a closure.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript course progress tracker that processes lesson scores and keeps track of how many lessons have been evaluated. Use an arrow function as a callback to transform the lesson scores into progress values. Then create a closure-based tracker function that remembers how many lessons have been processed between calls. Print the processed scores and the final number of processed lessons.
requirements: Store multiple lesson scores in an array.
Use an arrow function as a callback to process each score.
Use an array method that accepts a callback.
Create a closure that preserves a private counter between function calls.
Call the closure for every lesson that is processed.
Print the processed scores and processed lesson count.
objectives: Use arrow functions as callback functions.
Understand how callbacks are passed to array methods.
Create and use a closure with preserved lexical scope.
Combine callbacks and closures in a practical JavaScript program.
tasks.hint: Use map() with an arrow function to transform each score. For the closure, create a function that contains a private count variable and returns another function that increments and returns that count.
tasks.solutionExplanation: map() receives an arrow function callback and creates a new array from the lesson scores. createLessonTracker() contains processedCount inside its local scope and returns a function that can still access that variable after createLessonTracker() finishes. This preserved access is the closure. Each processed lesson calls trackLesson(), which increments the private counter.

tasks.title: Build a Course Progress Analyzer
tasks.description: Create a JavaScript course progress analyzer using objects, array methods, destructuring, spread and safe access with default values.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript program that analyzes several course lessons. Each lesson must contain a title and completion status. Use array methods to find the completed lessons, create a list of lesson titles, and calculate whether all required lessons are completed. Then create a new student profile from an existing object using spread syntax and safely read an optional profile city using optional chaining and nullish coalescing. Print the analysis results to the console.
requirements: Store lesson data as an array of objects.
Use filter() to find completed lessons.
Use map() to create a list containing lesson titles.
Use every() to determine whether all lessons are completed.
Use destructuring to extract a property from an object.
Use spread syntax to create an updated object without modifying the original object.
Use optional chaining and nullish coalescing to safely read a missing nested value.
Print all analysis results to the console.
objectives: Work with arrays containing objects.
Apply map(), filter() and every() to practical data.
Use destructuring for clean property access.
Use spread syntax for object transformation.
Safely handle optional nested data.
tasks.hint: Represent each lesson as an object such as { title, completed }. filter() can select completed lessons, map() can extract titles and every() can check whether every lesson is completed. Use const { name } = student to destructure and {...student, progress: newValue} to create an updated object.
tasks.solutionExplanation: filter() creates an array containing only completed lessons, while map() creates a new array containing lesson titles. every() returns true only when every lesson satisfies the completion condition. Destructuring extracts name from the student object. Spread creates updatedStudent as a new object while preserving the original values. Optional chaining safely checks address.city, and ?? supplies Unknown when the value is null or undefined.

tasks.solutionExplanation: Set removes duplicate student IDs because each value can appear only once. Map stores a student ID with its latest score, so the later s1 record replaces the earlier score. filter() selects passing records and reduce() calculates the total used for the average. Destructuring extracts selectedStudent properties, while spread creates updatedStudent without changing the original object. Optional chaining safely accesses profile.city and ?? provides Unknown when the city is unavailable.

tasks.hint: Create one AbortController and pass controller.signal to every fetch. Calling controller.abort() cancels requests using that signal. In catch, check error.name === 'AbortError' before handling other errors.
tasks.solutionExplanation: createCourseDashboardLoader creates one AbortController for the complete dashboard operation. Both fetch requests receive the same signal, so aborting the controller can cancel both requests. Promise.all allows the independent requests to run concurrently. Each response is checked with response.ok before its JSON body is read. The returned cancel function calls controller.abort(). If cancellation happens, fetch rejects with an AbortError, which is handled separately so the user receives a clear cancellation message. Other errors are handled as normal dashboard failures.

Understand how nested object references can cause accidental mutation.

requirements: Create a class named CoursePerformanceManager.
Store the course name and student records using this.
Create an addStudent() method that accepts a student name and numeric progress.
Throw an Error when the name is missing or progress is outside 0 to 100.

tasks.title: Build a Pure Student Progress Utility
tasks.description: Create a small reusable JavaScript utility for calculating and updating student course progress without mutating the original student data.
tasks.problemStatement: Create a JavaScript application for a learning platform. Organize the code into a reusable utility module and a main JavaScript file. In the utility module, create a pure function named calculateProgress(done, total) that returns the progress percentage and safely handles a total of zero. Also create a function named updateStudent(student, progress) that returns a new student object with the updated progress without changing the original student object. In the main file, create a student object, calculate the student's progress, create an updated student object, and print both the original and updated objects to the console so that the difference can be verified.
objectives: Organize JavaScript logic into a reusable module.
Create a pure function for calculating course progress.
Update student data without mutating the original object.
Use the returned values correctly from the main JavaScript file.
requirements: Create a separate JavaScript utility module for the reusable functions.
Export calculateProgress(done, total) from the utility module.
Return 0 when total is 0 instead of producing an invalid percentage.
Create updateStudent(student, progress) using an immutable object update.
Do not directly modify the original student's progress property.
Import the utility functions into the main JavaScript file.
Print the original student and updated student data to the console.
tasks.hint: Use export and import to separate the utility from the main file. calculateProgress can return total ? Math.round(done / total * 100) : 0. For updateStudent, create a new object with the spread operator, such as { ...student, progress }.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The reusable functions are placed in a separate module so the main file only coordinates the application. calculateProgress is a pure function because it only uses its arguments and does not modify external data. The total check prevents division by zero. updateStudent uses the spread operator to create a new object instead of changing the original student object. The console output shows that the original student remains unchanged while the new object contains the calculated progress.

Create immutable student updates.
Design functions that can be tested independently.

requirements: Create a separate module containing the reusable progress functions.
Create calculateProgress(done, total) with safe zero-total handling.
Create updateStudent(student, progress) without mutating the source object.
Reject progress values below 0 or above 100.
Write console.assert tests for normal progress calculation.
Test the zero-total edge case.
Test 100 percent completion.
Test invalid progress input.
Use debugger or console inspection while diagnosing a deliberately incorrect calculation.
Fix the bug and leave the final implementation passing all tests.

tasks.description: Build a modular course progress service that combines immutability, testing, debugging, safe DOM updates, explicit error handling and production-quality validation.
tasks.problemStatement: Build a small production-style course progress application for a learning platform. Organize the application into reusable JavaScript modules. Create pure functions for calculating progress and creating updated student records without mutation. Validate incoming student and progress data and throw meaningful errors for invalid values. Add assertions for the important business rules and use a debugger statement or DevTools inspection point during development. Create a browser page that displays the student's course information from JavaScript and update the DOM using textContent so user-provided values cannot be interpreted as HTML. The final implementation must keep responsibilities separated, handle errors explicitly, avoid accidental mutation, and remain readable and maintainable.
objectives: Design a maintainable multi-module JavaScript application.
Use pure functions and immutable data updates.
Validate external or user-provided values before using them.
Test important business rules with assertions.
Debug application behavior using browser DevTools.
Render dynamic data safely with textContent.
Apply production-oriented readability, error handling and security practices.
requirements: Separate the application into modules with clear responsibilities.
Create a pure function that calculates course progress safely.
Create an immutable student update function.
Validate that the student name and course name are non-empty strings.
Validate that progress is a number between 0 and 100.
Throw meaningful errors when invalid data is supplied.
Write console.assert tests for progress calculation and validation rules.
Include at least one edge-case test.
Use debugger or DevTools inspection while developing the application.
Create DOM elements for the student name, course name and progress.
Use textContent for dynamic student and course values.
Do not use innerHTML for user-provided values.
Keep business logic separate from DOM rendering logic.
Handle errors explicitly instead of silently ignoring them.
Keep the final code readable, modular and maintainable.
tasks.hint: Keep validation and business logic in a service module and DOM rendering in a separate module. A validation function can check typeof value === 'string' and value.trim().length > 0. Dynamic values are written with textContent instead of innerHTML, so values supplied by a student are treated as text rather than HTML. Validation prevents invalid student and progress data from entering the application. Assertions verify important rules and the debugger can be used during development to inspect unexpected values. Errors are caught explicitly and reported through console.error. This structure makes the application easier to test, debug, secure and maintain.

tasks.solutionExplanation: The solution uses separate modules for API access, progress calculation, state management and DOM rendering. loadCourse() handles asynchronous API access and validates both HTTP status and the basic course structure. The state uses a Set so completing the same lesson twice does not create duplicate progress.
